headline: PAGASA Raises Red Rainfall Warning Across Much of Central Luzon as Habagat Flood Risk Intensifies
seoTitle: Red Rainfall Warning Across Central Luzon | FMB News
seoDescription: PAGASA placed Zambales, Bataan, Pampanga and Bulacan under red rainfall warnings on August 29 as Habagat rains raised serious flooding risks.
deck: Serious flooding remained a threat as monsoon rains intensified across western and central Luzon on Saturday.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: PAGASA maintained red rainfall warnings over Zambales, Bataan, Pampanga and Bulacan on Saturday, August 29, as the southwest monsoon continued to bring intense rain and serious flooding risk across parts of Luzon.
By 11:00 a.m., the red-warning area had expanded to include Metro Manila and parts of Tarlac, Batangas, Cavite and Rizal. PAGASA's warning means serious flooding is expected in flood-prone areas.

sections.heading: Weather setup
paragraphs: PAGASA's early-morning forecast placed a low-pressure area about 520 kilometers north-northeast of Itbayat, Batanes, while the southwest monsoon remained the dominant rain-producing system over western Luzon.
The bureau warned that flash floods and landslides remain possible where heavy to intense rain falls over already saturated ground.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: Rainfall-warning coverage can change within hours as radar observations update. Residents should rely on the latest PAGASA regional heavy-rainfall warning rather than an older warning map when making safety decisions.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: Repeated heavy rain over Central Luzon increases the risk of river flooding, urban inundation and slope failures even after rainfall temporarily weakens.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: PAGASA continues issuing three-hour heavy-rainfall warnings and broader weather advisories. Local disaster offices may order evacuations or road closures as conditions change.
